scope: Proposition 8.2 of the manuscript “Midpoint lenses in segment spaces” (preprints/Midpoint-lenses-in-segment-spaces-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 331 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e5fa3ffa1ac9778a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let I be countable and let (hi)i∈I be nonnegative integers. On the disjoint forest Fh = ∐︂ i∈I ({i} × N≤hi ) define Jh by the same disjoint-segment norm and set Xh = J∗ h. If J(h) denotes the single-tree completion on N≤h, then Jh = (︂ ⨁︂ i∈I J(hi) )︂ ℓ2 , Xh = (︂ ⨁︂ i∈I J(hi)∗ )︂ ℓ2 isometrically under coordinate restriction. Both spaces are reflexive, and finite coordinate vectors are dense in each. The projection and complementary-subtree formulas remain valid for this forest. The convention of one tree with n levels, including the root, for every n ≥ 1 gives exactly Jlevels = R ⊕2 J, Xlevels = R ⊕2 X. Its component estimate is ∥u∥2 ≤ ρ(u) ≤ √ n ∥u∥2, and a root-to-leaf path has n − 1 extension steps.
